title: Trace where a mesh request succeeds or stops
description: Switch scenarios to compare configuration distribution with the live request path. Select any component to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Caller workload
nodes.detail: Starts the request and owns its business deadline, idempotency contract, fallback, and interpretation of the final response.

nodes.label: Outbound enforcer
nodes.detail: Discovers an endpoint, applies client-side route and retry policy, and presents the caller workload identity to a meshed peer.

nodes.label: Mesh control plane
nodes.detail: Combines service discovery, identity, and policy, then distributes configuration. It is not a synchronous hop in the application request.

nodes.label: Inbound enforcer
nodes.detail: Authenticates the presented peer identity, evaluates destination authorization, records network evidence, and forwards only allowed traffic.

nodes.label: Orders workload
nodes.detail: Owns order validation, durable state, business authorization, and correctness. A successful proxy hop does not prove the order operation is correct.

nodes.label: Telemetry pipeline
nodes.detail: Receives bounded metrics, traces, and access logs. It should not be required to acknowledge each request before the application can respond.

scenarios.label: Healthy request
scenarios.summary: Both enforcement points have accepted current configuration and the caller identity is authorized for the destination operation.
scenarios.result: The request follows the data plane and reaches the Orders workload. Control-plane distribution and telemetry export are related paths, not synchronous application hops.

scenarios.label: Control plane down
scenarios.summary: The control plane is unavailable after both data-plane components accepted a usable configuration snapshot.
scenarios.result: Existing traffic can continue with the last accepted state in this model. New discovery, policy, or identity changes may be delayed or fail, so operators must restore the control plane before relying on a rollout.

scenarios.label: Policy denies
scenarios.summary: The caller has a valid mesh identity, but the destination policy does not allow that identity to perform this operation.
scenarios.result: The inbound enforcement point rejects the request and records the decision. The Orders workload is not reached; authentication succeeded, while authorization failed.

scenarios.label: Unmeshed caller
scenarios.summary: A caller reaches the destination network path without a workload identity accepted by the strict destination policy.
scenarios.result: The strict destination rejects the call before the application. Roll out strict enforcement only after every legitimate caller can present an accepted identity.

scenarios.label: Outbound proxy fails
scenarios.summary: The caller's outbound traffic enforcement point is unavailable, even though the control plane and destination remain healthy.
scenarios.result: The request cannot leave the caller through the modeled mesh path. Data-plane health is an application availability dependency and needs resource limits, probes, dashboards, and a tested recovery path.
